extracted.intended_audience: early-career tenure-track assistant professors and university research administrators (limited-submission coordinators)
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Searle Scholars Program: who is eligible, what types of research it funds, the award size and term, and that it is a limited-submission institutional program. Useful for potential applicants and institutional grant officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited submission award program
rubrics_metrics.description: The Searle Scholars Program is a limited submission award program that makes grants to selected academic and research institutions to support the independent research of outstanding early-career scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because it is a limited-submission program, institutions (not individual applicants directly) must follow internal selection/nomination processes to put forward candidates for the award. The program awards grants to selected institutions rather than open direct application by unlimited individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — appointment and career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports 'outstanding early-career scientists who have recently been appointed as assistant professors on a tenure-track appointment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is limited to individuals who are assistant professors on a tenure-track (i.e., early-career faculty) and who have been 'recently appointed' — the program targets very early-stage faculty. Institutions should confirm appointment status and recency when selecting nominees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for independent research
rubrics_metrics.description: The program 'makes grants ... to support the independent research' of selected early-career scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees are expected to pursue their own independent research programs rather than supporting work primarily directed by senior collaborators; institutional nominations should emphasize the nominee's independence and capacity to lead a research program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research emphasis — high risk, high reward
rubrics_metrics.description: The Searle Scholars Program 'supports high risk, high reward research' across disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program favors innovative, potentially transformative projects that carry higher risk; nomination materials should highlight novelty, potential impact, and the ambitious nature of proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary scope — broad range of scientific disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: The program funds work 'across a broad range of scientific disciplines.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is not restricted to a single field; nominees may come from diverse scientific areas. Institutions should consider strong early-career candidates across life sciences and related scientific disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant size and term
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are '$450,000 for a three-year term with $150,000 payable each year of the grant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award budget and disbursement schedule are fixed as stated; proposals and institutional planning should align project scope and budgets with the $150,000/year funding level over three years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration and funding source
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is 'administered by Kinship Foundation and is funded through the Searle Funds at the Chicago Community Trust.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies program administrators and funders for purposes of institutional coordination, reporting expectations, and points of contact; not an applicant evaluation criterion but relevant program logistics.
